$comment: Autoscaling rules for the api service. Used by `npm run autoscale`; every value can be overridden
connections  WebSocket connections held by a replica
cpu          percent of ONE core, from the process's own cpuUsage()
memory       resident set size in MB (absolute — a percentage needs a limit)
rpm          HTTP requests per minute, over a short sliding window. Excludes
/api/health: the autoscaler polls it to find replicas, and a metric
that rises when you measure it climbs to max on its own.
up/down: watermarks in that signal's units. Leave a wide gap between them, or the two touch and
aggregate: mean (default) | max. `max` scales on the hottest replica, which is usually right for
cpu — one saturated event loop is a real problem even when the mean looks calm.
proportional: whether the signal redistributes when a replica leaves. Used only by the anti-flap
check. True for connections and cpu; false for memory, because a departing replica's
baseline heap goes away with it rather than moving to its neighbours.
Up if ANY rule wants up; down only if EVERY rule agrees — same as a Kubernetes HPA with several
metrics. The defaults below are deliberately low so the loop is observable on a demo stack; real
numbers would be in the thousands of connections.
